name: veterinary_clinic_system_068_patient_species_weight_sanity
instruction:
Run a species/weight sanity audit on the patients table. Use current veterinary references (AAHA/AAFP for canine and feline, avian/exotic/equine references for the others) to determine species-typical adult weight ranges in kilograms. Do not use any hardcoded ranges from prompts or seed files.

For every patient:
- If weight_kg is missing, set weight_flag='missing' (no weight_checked tag).
- If weight_kg is within the species-typical range, set weight_flag='plausible' (no tag).
- If weight_kg is strictly outside the species-typical range, set weight_flag='out_of_range' and weight_checked='<batch_code>'.

Then:
1. Push one ops_reports row per species plus an 'ALL' rollup report='weight_sanity' with batch_code, species, total, plausible, out_of_range, missing.
2. For every out_of_range patient, push one reminder_queue row kind='weight_recheck', status='queued', patient_id, message 'Patient <patient_id> weight out of species range - batch <batch_code>', queued_by='system', queued_at the episode timestamp.
3. Push one audit_log row: action='WEIGHT_SANITY_AUDIT', actor='system', actor_role='system', target_collection='patients', target_id='batch', details='Batch <batch_code> - weight sanity audit complete', occurred_at the episode timestamp.

Do not change weight_kg, species, or any other patient field.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: Every patient has weight_flag set to 'plausible', 'out_of_range', or 'missing'. out_of_range rows also have weight_checked=batch. ops_reports has one weight_sanity row per species plus an ALL rollup with counts matching live data. reminder_queue has one weight_recheck per out_of_range patient. audit_log has the batch entry. No other patient fields change.

checks.expect: exact weight_flag and weight_checked tag on every patient
per-species and ALL counts agree between Python filter and SQL GROUP BY/CASE

hazards: All 21 avian patients have weight_kg = 1.0 (e.g. ids 7, 23, 31, 38, 95, 100, 106, 112, 135, 150). The species-typical avian range must have an upper bound above 1.0; a wrong upper bound of 1.0 or less would flag every avian as out_of_range.
7 small canines are at 4-5 kg (ids 66, 144, 146, 166, 201, 205, 264). The canine lower bound must be at or below 4 kg; a lower bound above 4 would misclassify these as out_of_range.
16 equine patients range from 398 kg to 518 kg (e.g. id 211 is 398 kg). The equine lower bound must be at or below 398; a common equine 'adult' lower bound of 400 kg would flag id 211.
All 300 patients have a non-null weight_kg, so missing=0. A solution that sets any weight_flag='missing' on a non-null weight fails.
Canine, feline, exotic, and avian ranges are very different; a solution that applies the canine range to all species or ignores species will misclassify the non-canine patients.
